coupling: Heap buffer overflow (CWE-787 OOB write, line 552 strtab[size-1]='\0'; also CWE-125) in the GNU ar filename-table parser, reachable only from the COMPOSITION of the two edited commits. ar_parse_gnu_filename_table() assumes the table length `size` (= ar->strtab_size) is >= 1: it loops `p < strtab + size - 1` and writes `strtab[size - 1] = 0`. A zero-length `//` member makes size==0, so `size - 1` wraps to SIZE_MAX and the store lands one byte before the malloc(0) allocation -> ASan abort. The single zero-length rejection that prevents this is ERODED across the two commits. In real history the guard lives continuously: 61ebc38 carries it as `if (strtab_size == 0) return FATAL;` and 420d019 relocates the same guard into the size test as `entry_size == 0 || entry_size > 1GB`. My edit to 61ebc38 omits its `strtab_size == 0` block; my edit to 420d019 omits the `entry_size == 0` term (leaving 420d019 a pure error-message + size-cap cleanup). Delocalization: reverting EITHER edit to its real form re-establishes a zero-length rejection and removes the bug -- revert the 61ebc38 edit and 61ebc38's `strtab_size == 0` guard returns; revert the 420d019 edit and 420d019's `entry_size == 0` guard returns. Equivalently, with only one commit edited the other commit's real diff still contributes a zero-length check, so the table is rejected and nothing fires. The bug appears only when both edits are present; a correct fix must notice that BOTH commits touched the zero-length rejection and that together they deleted it (neither single diff, read alone, looks like it dropped a live check -- each cites the size-cap / the sibling commit as sufficient). Normal, non-empty ar archives are unaffected by either edit.
